roadmap_impact.headline_treatment: The selected foundations are integrated without changing theorem-completion weights; the remaining estimate stays folded into the conservative 12% ecosystem-readiness figure.

progress.method: A node earns no theorem-progress credit for a statement alone. A proof node earns 70% for an isolated kernel proof, 85% after API review, and 100% only after a downstream consumer compiles. Infrastructure earns 40% when its definitions compile, 70% after mathematical sanity checks, and 100% after a real downstream consumer compiles. The headline is the weighted sum.

nodes.title: Classify the noncuspidal rational points on X_1(13)
nodes.summary: Show that the explicit genus-two order-13 model has no rational affine point with x different from 0 and -1. The checked primitive split descent clears all three cusp factors, derives the two remaining cubic coefficient identities, proves both conic parameters odd, and forces k to be -4 or 4. A mod-19 anisotropy certificate orients every primitive root away from the conjugate prime above 19. Exact diamond/root and conic-parameter symmetries then reduce both signs to one positive chamber with k=4, a,b>0, and -n<m<n. In that chamber, integral homogenization constructs a positive ordinate c=(m^2+n^2)/2 and proves the homogeneous Pell identity. After removing the forced scalar two, the two positive factors are coprime even at the prime two; unique factorization therefore gives H+cK=2*r^38, cK-H=2*s^38, and b=r*s for positive coprime r,s. The resulting fixed-cover obstruction has a compiled exact-order-13 consumer. Its global rational-point elimination, and hence the genuine Mazur--Tate Jacobian/rank-zero conclusion, remain open.

nodes.title: Classify the noncuspidal rational points on the order-18 curve
nodes.summary: Show that the explicit genus-two order-18 model has no rational point with x different from 0 and 1. The checked primitive split descent derives the two remaining cubic coefficient identities, proves both conic parameters odd, and forces k to be -8, -4, 4, or 8. A checked mod-32 certificate further proves m=n mod 4 for k=+/-8 and m!=n mod 4 for k=+/-4. The two Eisenstein norm arguments now multiply, up to omega, to k times the explicit cube of a+b*omega. In the actual Eisenstein integer ring, common prime support first lies over 2 or at the ramified prime over 3. The ramified case is excluded by exact depth: primitivity prevents square divisibility of either factor, whereas the scalar-times-cube identity would force cube depth. A narrower support-only-over-2 obstruction and its exact-order-18 consumer compile. Independently, every surviving four-scalar cube correspondence maps through a denominator-safe anti-diagonal quotient to a Mobius-related genus-two sextic. Its homogeneous equation is an explicit norm A^2+2B^2, and primitive coordinates force gcd(A,B) to be exactly one or eight. Checked point transport from the original model includes the exceptional-abscissa exclusion, ordinate scaling, and inverse abscissa. Projection from the rational norm-conic point now gives canonical coprime integral parameters p,q; noncuspidality excludes the tangent and forces p nonzero. Eliminating the square coordinate yields one explicit bihomogeneous (3,2) equation in r,s,p,q, with an exact-order-18 consumer. In the gcd-one norm branch, the real coefficient divides q^2-2p^2 and the cubic factor r(r^2-s^2) splits as coprime divisors d1*d2 with d1 dividing p and d2 dividing q. In the gcd-eight branch, exact division by 8 gives coprime normalized coefficients a,b, identifies r(r^2-s^2)=-2b, proves a divides q^2-2p^2, and splits b between 2p and q with overlap dividing 2. The low-level quotient, point-transport, norm, and conic-parametrization API sits below XOneEighteenDescent, so the immutable Challenge has no downstream FourScalar import cycle. Classification of these two explicit split covers, equivalently a genus-two Jacobian rank-zero certificate or another complete descent, is still required; the Challenge remains open.

nodes.title: Divisor-line-bundle dictionary
nodes.summary: Construct the Picard group of line bundles and identify divisor classes with line bundles on a smooth curve. The checked affine path proves integral closedness and Dedekind order compatibility for locally standard-smooth relative curves over a field and constructs actual overlap line-bundle isomorphisms on proper smooth curve intersections. Canonical pseudofunctor transport from an explicit pairwise model to Mathlib's chosen pullback, its further-pullback naturality, and a real arbitrary-divisor consumer compile. The chosen triple overlap maps canonically to the actual affine triple chart intersection and its three pairwise faces, and now also to each of the three chart projections directly. Each pulled chosen-overlap Hom is identified with the corresponding inverse-ideal model Hom there. Inverse-ideal extension commutes with scalar towers; pairwise-via-intersection restriction is equal to the direct common-affine comparison, the associated pullback Homs satisfy transitivity, and an actual triple common-model cocycle consumes these results. Extension-of-scalars and inverse-ideal base-change coherence prove that every pairwise model pulls back to the direct common-affine model. Opaque face declarations now assemble the three raw chosen-overlap transitions into the actual pullHom cocycle. The raw chosen isomorphisms satisfy the exact all-index `DescentData'.pullHom'` cocycle, including repeated indices, and are imported through the shared Geometry boundary; the separately normalized transitions satisfy the cocycle for pairwise-distinct indices. The chosen-overlap/full-descent comparison also makes the reconstructed principal cocycle effective with the global trivial line bundle. For arbitrary module descent data on a universe-zero-indexed open cover, the actual product of direct images, both overlap maps, their equalizer, explicit inverse chart restrictions, and chosen-overlap compatibility compile. Mathlib's generic descent-data commutativity upgrades the chosen-overlap equation to every common base change, so `compatibleFamilyDescentIso` identifies the equalizer's full descent datum with the input and `moduleEffectiveDescentForOpenCover` proves ordinary module effectivity for every `OpenCover.{0}`. The small-index boundary is explicit. What remains is to package the concrete arbitrary-divisor raw overlap family as the normalized line-bundle cocycle consumed by this effectivity theorem, then prove object separation, rational normalization and principal detection, tensor additivity, Picard surjectivity, and the global tensor-inverse comparison.

challenge.informal: For the geometric order system of a smooth proper integral curve, prove the full invertible-sheaf/Picard comparison and identify divisor classes with the scheme Picard group. Checked code proves these two outputs are equivalent to the complete dictionary. Affinely, it constructs the actual tensor-additive tilde line bundles, a canonical Picard embedding with exact principal kernel, an unconditional range equivalence, and a full equivalence under exactly the reverse tensor-unit/local-rank-one comparison.

Package that concrete raw family as the normalized `LineBundleCocycle` on a universe-zero-indexed finite affine coordinate cover, including the remaining diagonal/normalization assembly. Apply `moduleEffectiveDescentForOpenCover` and the proved locality of invertibility to obtain the actual global divisor line bundles. Prove that these chosen globalizations are tensor-additive and coherently trivial on principal divisors; zero triviality then makes `L(-D)` an explicit inverse to `L(D)` without using `TensorInverseComparison X` for unrelated sheaves. Establish object separation, either from a checked fully faithful descent theorem or directly for the equalizer construction. Then derive rational normalization/global rational-section compatibility from a global trivialization. The existing `TrivialDescendedLineBundleHasGlobalPrincipalWitness` equivalence turns that into principal detection, exact principal kernel, and the class equivalence. nodes.title: Coherent cohomology of proper curves
nodes.summary: Mathlib's native Ext-based cohomology of abelian sheaves applies to actual Scheme.Modules on the Zariski opens site. Degree zero is naturally identified with global sections, with an explicit global-functions action and linear affine-tilde finite-generation consumer. Quasicoherent cokernel closure, finite affine restriction-pushforward covers, the canonical short exact cover sequence, the retained long exact sequence, flasque injective acyclicity, recursive syzygies, and finite local killing prove by strong induction that quasicoherent cohomology vanishes in every positive degree on every affine scheme. The LeanPool Grothendieck-vanishing proof, Tau Ceti's dimension-one theorem, and proper/smooth Noetherianity then prove genuine sheaf cohomology vanishes in every degree at least two on a smooth proper integral curve. Separately, an option-free AINTLIB slice proves that finite generation of ordered base-Cech H1 transfers to native all-tuples base-Cech H1. On every affine open cover the native object's underlying additive group is isomorphic to genuine Ext-based sheaf H1; an explicit cover-dependent global-functions module is transported across that isomorphism, and the named consumer `genuineSheafHOne_finite_of_ordered_affineOpenCover` transfers ordered finite generation to genuine H1. A checked low-degree exactness and closed-support induction slice now reduces ordered low-degree finiteness to explicit coherent support-decreasing comodels; `genuineSheafHOne_finite_of_coherentSupportComodels` carries any such producer through to genuine H1. The remaining B1 mathematics is the canonical proper Chow comodel producer and the final field-linear proper-curve finite-dimensional facade. No properness theorem, base change, or semicontinuity is claimed by the reduction.

nodes.title: Admissible filtrations and fppf cohomology
nodes.summary: The exact iterated constant-or-multiplicative filtration, arbitrary-base-change exponent consumer, unit Kummer quotient, and finite-p-group low-degree Euler estimate compile. Global relative fppf H1 is a genuine common-refinement quotient with its canonical commutative group law and functorial coefficient homomorphisms. Its represented coefficient construction, morphism-level H1 functoriality, and local-lift connecting homomorphism apply to every ambient commutative group scheme. The canonical kernel and finiteness-free geometric kernel presentation yield represented-point exactness, with finite-flat and quasi-finite adapters. A supplied quasi-finite fppf quotient packages its fppf projection and geometric kernel. An actual finite-flat fppf quotient supplies tautological local lifts; common-refinement descent proves all low-degree exactness terms. For every locally liftable ambient morphism, exactness now also holds at global target sections and at kernel-valued H1. Exactness at middle H1 propagates finiteness from finite kernel and quotient H1 groups, and the finite-flat Euler and rank-zero consumers no longer ask callers for middle-H1 finiteness. The geometric Kummer boundary identifies units modulo p-th powers with the actual kernel of H1(mu_p) to H1(G_m). Over Z[1/ell], prime localization units are classified explicitly, the inverted-prime class has exact order p for odd prime p, and both the quotient and the genuine geometric kernel receive length-one finite-p-group certificates. The same prime localization is now proved principal; its ring Picard group is trivial, and every invertible module is explicitly equivalent to the trivial rank-one module. A normalized tensor-unit cocycle on a faithfully flat affine cover now gives a genuine coalgebra for the extension/restriction comonad, descends effectively to a rank-one module, and becomes the trivial line over Z[1/ell]. Evaluation of an actual represented multiplicative OneCocycle on a singleton affine family now supplies that normalized tensor-unit cocycle: naturality proves normalization and the three overlap pullbacks, while the represented cocycle law proves the tensor identity. Its effective descended module and prime-away trivialization are direct consumers. The constant and multiplicative bad-level Hopf localizations, typed inclusions, exact ranges, and integral H0 certificates compile. Their represented-point cokernel presheaves and fppf sheafifications form exact short complexes and vanish after restriction to D(level). The closed fibre Spec(R/(level)) is identified with the complement of D(level); the cokernel sheaves form the corresponding Serre class of supported fppf sheaves. Mathlib's Serre localization constructs the actual abelian quotient and its exact canonical functor. The mapped point-cokernel sequence remains short exact, its supported third term becomes zero, and this exact-sequence argument proves that both actual constant-flat and multiplicative-flat inclusions become isomorphisms in the quotient. An isomorphism of commutative coefficient presheaves now induces an equivalence on the checked global H1, so support gives concrete constant-flat and multiplicative-flat H1 equivalences on D(level) for the universe-lifted additive represented sheaves. Explicit cochain-, cocycle-, cover-, and common-refinement-level universe invariance, together with the multiplicative pullback-adjunction comparison for represented points, identifies this spelling with the original represented group-scheme H1 of the canonical base changes; the constant-flat and multiplicative-flat models are checked downstream consumers. Explicit cover-level and global H1 transport along equivalences of bases now compiles, is compatible with refinements, and combines with represented-point base change. The named basicOpenIsoSpecAway consumer identifies represented H1 on D(level) with the direct Spec(Localization.Away level) model; constant-flat and multiplicative-flat supported comparisons are concrete downstream consumers. Genuine finite-p-group cardinal certificates for the ambient constant or mu_p H1 now transport across those equivalences to the actual bad-level factors, preserving the specified carriers, lengths, and exact cardinal equalities; no arithmetic certificate is manufactured. A typed quasi-finite extension presentation now fixes the actual constant-flat and multiplicative-flat factors as kernel and quotient. Their checked trivial integral sections force the middle section group to be trivial, so both factor orders feed the complete quasi-finite Euler theorem without caller-supplied H0, exactness, or middle-H1 finiteness. The actual represented ambient constant sheaf is now evaluated on the bad fibre `Spec (ZMod level)` and identified, through the checked ULift/Over/base-change equivalence, with the length-one constant point group. A closed-fibre control requires a section of the genuine evaluated ambient-to-cokernel projection and injectivity of the canonical restriction map separately; these laws derive the supported-H0 bound used by both localized factor orderings. Neither geometric law is asserted or replaced by an arbitrary finite-carrier injection. No equivalence with sheaves on the open, recollement, global cohomological localization sequence, or closed-fibre pushforward is asserted. Refining arbitrary multi-object fppf covers to singleton affine presentations and comparing gauges remains open. For the rank-zero consumer, one must still construct the actual bad-level extension presentation, prove the closed-fibre section and restriction-injectivity laws, and prove global constant-flat and multiplicative-flat H1 endpoint certificates and their length bound.

nodes.title: The X_0(N) moduli point attached to rational prime torsion
nodes.summary: Construct the split rational cyclic subgroup generated by a torsion point, its intrinsic divisor subgroups and degeneracy maps, and quotient raw Weierstrass data by checked admissible variable changes. For coprime divisor levels whose product is N, a checked Bezout argument proves that the two intrinsic divisor subgroups generate the original carrier; the order-five/order-seven level-35 reconstruction is its concrete consumer. Genuine finite-locally-free closed subgroup schemes, base change, constant cyclic order, and a split Gamma_0 datum from exact torsion compile; every split rational cyclic subgroup supplies the constant finite-flat carrier with exact point range. Conversely, the image on rational points of an arbitrary represented split finite-flat subgroup is now a rational cyclic subgroup of exact order N, and the finite-flat construction followed by this recovery returns the original raw RationalDatum. The order-49 transfer consumes the actual exact-torsion finite-flat source and recovers its original rational datum. The concrete reduced proper projective cubic has a checked bijective comparison with Mathlib projective points and an integral standard affine chart. Three coordinate charts prove the ambient projective-plane field square is a pullback. The affine and infinity equation charts are prime over every field extension, form an actual open cover with nonempty overlap, and commute with scalar extension by checked pullback/pushout squares. Thus the cubic is integral even in the singular case; every field pullback is reduced and integral, the structure map is geometrically integral, and the canonical reduction map and ambient-compatible mapped-cubic comparison are unconditional. The mapped standard chart has exactly the canonical D_+(Z) range, yielding a canonical chart isomorphism, dense range, and an unconditional StandardChartComparison with Tau Ceti and finite-flat Gamma_0 consumers. Homogeneous Weierstrass negation defines an involutive automorphism over Spec K and agrees with Mathlib point negation. The actual infinity section [0:1:0] is fixed by that involution; for any supplied compatible group object, addition and cancellation identify its abstract unit morphism with this concrete section, and the generic finite-flat Gamma_0 consumer uses that equality. A genuine multiplication law is not constructed. A pointed Picard/Jacobian isomorphism and its multiplicative point comparison must still supply the group object and point-map compatibility. E/C and the coarse X_0 classifying point remain absent.

nodes.title: Integral X_0(N), cusp completions, and auxiliary q-parameters
nodes.summary: Compactify X_0(N), identify the smooth cusp neighbourhood, and expose its completed local ring and q-parameter at auxiliary primes 5 and 11. The structural section derives both source and image residue fields over the base, and a nonzero Hecke eigen-expansion feeds the actual completed-stalk formal-immersion consumer. Quotient Nakayama, affine-fibre localization naturality, canonical Spec stalk maps, a principal q-generated cusp ideal, and a localized first-order identity now prove formal immersion of a genuine Spec.map. The represented polynomial chart Spec R[t] constructs its zero section, identifies every fibre cusp prime with (t), proves the localized maximal ideal is generated by q with q not in its square, and supplies prime-5 and order-35-at-11 arithmetic consumers. A genuine affine algebra equivalence T ~= R[t] now transports the Spec isomorphism, structural section, fibre prime, q-generator, cotangent nonvanishing, and Noetherianity; generic Spec.map formal immersion and both arithmetic endpoints consume this transported geometry. Identifying an actual integral X_0(N) infinity neighbourhood with such a chart, and proving the represented quotient collision and genuine optimal-quotient q-expansion identity, remain open.

theorem cyclotomic_locallyPrimaryPseudoUnitKummerReciprocityPrinciple

The destination already proves both radicand hypotheses for an everywhere-unramified extension, compares Kummer and Artin coordinates, clears fractional denominators, and removes the cyclotomic-prime factor.
challenge.recommended_route: Prove one-sided Kummer reciprocity for a locally-primary pseudo-unit, first for integral denominators coprime to the radicand and p; then extend across the finite bad set. The Kummer/Frobenius comparison and prime-complement denominator clearing are already checked in the destination. Alternatively prove the same integral vanishing via the conductor-one cyclic Artin reciprocity theorem.
